verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere ships official SDKs: one C++ core with six thin bindings. First-party docs cover the Swift SDK (streaming, chat, tool calling, structured output, STT/TTS, VLM, models), the Kotlin SDK and a React Native integration path, and the SDKs are published on GitHub. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of building with the SDKs, and documentation evidence for all six bindings (only Swift, Kotlin and React Native are shown).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: One C++ core, six thin bindings. Behaviour that does not drift between platforms.
The RunAnywhere Kotlin SDK runs language, speech, and vision models on the device.
The SDK owns the call-and-execute loop and detects the format the model expects.
The complete integration path for adding on-device LLM, STT, and TTS to a React Native app with the RunAnywhere SDK
